messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for dedicated pool eu-west-1.pool-42. Metric window: last 5m. p95=420ms p99=3.8s. Streaming stalls reported. Auto-scaler handshake delays observed. Paging on-call.
maria-ops: I'm on it. seeing a big backlog on queue: depth ~1.1k for pool-42. Customers hitting streaming stalls and aborted streams. tagging @ajay-sre for deep-dive.
ajay-sre: taking. grabbing pool runtime metrics now. running quick query:
```
# internal metrics
sum(rate(pool_requests_total{pool="eu-west-1.pool-42"}[1m])) by (status)
redwood_pool_warmup_pending{pool="eu-west-1.pool-42"} = 18
pool_queue_depth{pool="eu-west-1.pool-42"} = 1142
autoscaler_handshake_delay_seconds{pool="eu-west-1.pool-42"} avg = 6.4
```
ajay-sre: handshake_delay looks high (6s avg), warmup_pending nodes 18. autoscaler hasn't finished bringing nodes up fast enough. likely cold KV/cache plus streaming tail causing p99 blowout.
tom-eng: any server-side errors? logs show repeated handshake timeouts in node-provisioner:
```
2026-03-15T10:01:12Z provisioner: handshake timeout for slot S-197. reason=queue_surge
2026-03-15T10:02:09Z runtime: streaming stall detected request_id=abc123 path=/v1/stream
```
maria-ops: customer impact: at least 3 customers reporting degraded streaming (AcmeApp, TidalWare, BrightInbox). CS triage: streams either stall mid-response or take >5s at p99.
emily-cs: notifying AcmeApp account team and posting status. they saw a spike in dropped frames and player buffering. escalation email sent.
ajay-sre: immediate mitigation plan:
- divert new traffic for high-throughput routes to eu-west-1.pool-7 (failover pool) via routing policy.
- enable streaming fallback that disables continuous batching for affected routes.
- manually allocate 4 hotshot nodes into pool-42 to reduce queue and pre-warm.
nate-ops: I can do manual scale. running command:
```
redwoodctl pools allocate --pool eu-west-1.pool-42 --hotshot 4 --reason "incident: manual burst"
```
nate-ops: allocation accepted. new nodes provisioning; ETA warm ~70s.
ajay-sre: meanwhile enable fallback routing for heavy streaming models:
```
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/stream --fallback-pool eu-west-1.pool-7 --max-batch-size 8
```
kelsey-pm: will notify impacted product leads and update incident doc. adding severity=P1 and will coordinate postmortem owner.
tom-eng: observed that pool-7 is at ~60% capacity but can absorb most streaming burst if we reduce batch sizes. changing streaming mode to chunked to reduce tail latency.

-- 6310001285 --

maria-ops: quick telemetry after routing change and manual scale:
- queue_depth pool-42 -> 420 (was 1142)
- p95 -> 160ms (was 420ms)
- p99 -> 480ms (was 3.8s)
- streaming error_rate -> down from 2.7% to 0.4%
:thumbsup: good immediate improvement.

ajay-sre: digging into root cause hints: a large onboarding job from a new customer started a parallelized burst that pinned many KV shards, causing cold cache pressure and prolonging warmup times. autoscaler is configured with a conservative handshake timeout to avoid flapping; that setting caused it to wait before activating new slots.
sre-bot: Note: autoscaler config: min_handshake_timeout_seconds=5, max_parallel_warmups=6. Current observed handshake latencies exceeded threshold during H/A window.

ajay-sre: next actions:
- short-term: reduce handshake timeout to 3s to allow faster fallback to hotshot pool (apply cautiously).
- mid-term: implement predictive warmup for onboarding bursts (use request-rate signal to pre-warm based on rate-of-change).
- postmortem: analyze KV shard hotness and propose shard rebalancing or cache warming strategy.

nate-ops: reducing handshake timeout now for pool-42 to 3s (manual override). command executed.

-- 6310001320 --

maria-ops: after timeout tweak and with nodes online, we see p99 ~320ms and streaming stalls near zero. will keep monitoring for 30m. removing paging to broader SRE rotation but keeping on-call assigned.
ajay-sre: logging mitigation runbook steps and relevant metrics to incident doc. will open a follow-up ticket for autoscaler param staging and a canary rollout plan for lower handshake timeout.
kelsey-pm: assigning follow-up owner @tom-eng for shard rebalancing investigation and @ajay-sre for autoscaler tuning.
emily-cs: CS updated customers with ETA for full recovery and noted that streaming interruptions were mitigated; they request a postmortem and timeline we can share.
maria-ops: handoff to next on-call @ajay-sre at 10:25Z. summary for handoff:
- root issue: burst onboarding job + cold KV causing warmup delay + conservative autoscaler handshake-> large queue + tail latency.
- mitigations applied: manual hotshot allocation (4 nodes), routing fallback to pool-7, reduced handshake timeout to 3s, switched streaming to chunked for affected routes.
- current status: p95/p99 within SLO; queue depth reduced; customers notified.

ajay-sre: taking handoff. I'll track follow-ups: autoscaler param change, predictive warmup experiment, shard rebalancing ticket. leaving channel for updates. :eyes:

maria-ops: closing channel for active paging. if anyone sees p99 >1s re-alert immediately. thanks everyone for fast coordination. :heart:

sre-bot: Incident resolved (temporary mitigations). Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0427. Postmortem owner: kelsey-pm. Follow-up tasks: ["autoscaler-timeout-canary", "predictive-warmup-poc", "kv-shard-hotness-analysis"]
